summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the confidential supply-chain data drop and building a product: a polling loop plus agents that recheck the launch plan, flag contradictions, and take approved real-world actions (emails, site questions).
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan says all ok while the Collector's Edition misses Sunday (art book overbooking, failed statues, 5,900 copies short) and game cards are short. Built and pushed a Today/Launch/Routines app with portal poller, site questions, approver routing and reconciled shipment tracking; sent real follow-up emails to Boise, PackRight, Pune and Karton. The latest tracking work (271 tests passing) is not yet committed.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no notifications or webhooks. Files are replaced under the same name without notice, so polling must compare SHA-256 checksums, not just filenames.
Confidential data lives in gitignored data/ (and .env); .env.example is committed. Never commit data values or put them in code.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist; claim work with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md. Entire records checkpoints only when repo files change.
Book stock = last physical count + goods receipts - consumption, where consumption is backflushed from the pack-out log (packed copies x BOM parts). Only 'Last count' is real.

soony/erp/open_shipments.csv is the system export used by the app and froze at Fri 20 Nov 17:00. The hand-kept Excel tracker (open_shipments_tracker_v37_FINAL_final2.xlsx) was read only by the verifier until the tracking builder made it an evidence source.
Supplier contact names are in supplier profiles; the app greets by full profile name without a title, so hand-written emails must do the same.
The recognizer reads PDFs/images but not Word files, so the CPO memo (.docx) remains unread.
Parallel builders editing the same files (api.py, launch_view.py) prevent clean partial commits; commit only after all report.

code.finding: A later `_MONEY` regex in api.py overrides an earlier same-named one; the new cost-from-text regex had to be renamed to avoid the collision.
Routing/sign-off decisions must be evaluated after the final card status is known (approved vs half-done open), otherwise the rule fires too early.
silent_shipments measured silence against the newest list entry rather than the clock, so a frozen list made every shipment look fresh; tracking.py now measures against the clock using all sources.
Routines read only numeric cost fields, so options whose cost was only stated in text (e.g. 'about EUR 16,800') were treated as free; costs are now parsed from text.

workflow: The user granted standing permission for small paid image-recognition calls; saved in memory (ask-before-spending.md) so they need not be re-asked.
Real outward-facing actions (supplier emails, pushes) were confirmed with the user before sending; nothing was sent autonomously.
Subagents work well for large read-only cross-checks (200 order confirmations, 59 scans) and for parallel feature builds with separate file ownership.
Avoid sending multiple emails to one supplier within minutes; the brief warns that spammed suppliers may stop cooperating.
Verify rendered pages: the briefing artifact was published without a preview and needed a manual look.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, blocking all data access until the user supplied it.
Hand-written supplier emails guessed salutations ('Mr Nowak', 'Mr Rohan') from addresses; two were wrong.
Entire log showed a SessionStart under a different session ID and Codex hooks needing approval, which caused confusion about whether hooks fired.
Concurrent builders editing api.py made it impossible to commit my own changes separately.
Today list ordering was wrong: sleeve cards ranked above clear-case and art-book cards until ranking by launch impact was added.
Count cards (5) plus others add noise to Today; thresholds may need tuning.
open_items: Commit and restart with the tracking work (api.py, cardtools.py, launch_view.py, routines.py, tracking.py, tests, SupplyMap.tsx, api.ts), and read Megan's 06:36 Boise reply.
Send the Karton art book order (EUR 16,800, 8,000 books) only after Maren decides; the case is back on Today but nothing was sent.
Remaining audit fixes: separate the impacts.json write conflict between two agents; rank by real launch impact was done, verify others.
Read the CPO memo (.docx), which the recognizer cannot read.
Check possible double count of the 28,000 game cards (020-48113256) in the verifier and the floor.receipts() same-order-and-part issue.

Backend wishes from the routines UI: weekly would-handle count, per-action undo flag, shared look-alike grouping.
Update the briefing page and doc, which still show the 14:00 state; decide whether to delete the older Claude doc.
Prepare the office-hours question card for Nils at 09:00 (open_shipments.csv origin, receipt booking timing, backflush).
